bibliographic.title: Strategies and Pathways for Emerging Pollutant Governance Based on Artificial Intelligence Technology
bibliographic.authors: Chen Xiaohong, Liu Xiaoliang, Yuan Yige, An Qingxian
bibliographic.citation_apa: Chen, X., Liu, X., Yuan, Y., & An, Q. (2025). Strategies and pathways for emerging pollutant governance based on artificial intelligence technology. Chinese Engineering Science, 27(3), 152–159. https://doi.org/10.15302/J-SSCAE-2025.02.001

methodology.method_family: literature review and conceptual framework development
methodology.study_design: conceptual framework paper with narrative review
methodology.sector: environmental protection and emerging pollutant governance
methodology.technology_context: deep learning, natural language processing, machine learning, and large models applied to pollutant screening, risk assessment, monitoring, and control

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article focuses on environmental emerging-pollutant governance using AI and large models, not on conversational governance, chatbots, agents, or LLM oversight in regulated conversational systems.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text mentions artificial intelligence, large models, ChatGPT, governance, risk assessment, and monitoring, these refer to environmental pollutant management frameworks rather than governance of conversational LLM systems. No conversational AI, human oversight, guardrails, audit/logging for dialogue systems, or regulated-sector conversational deployment contexts appear in the provided text.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, and body; LLM references are ancillary to environmental pollutant management.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects only the provided excerpts. The paper presents a clear conceptual objective and AI-based pollutant governance framework, but offers no empirical sample, data collection protocol, or validated conversational/LLM governance evaluation relevant to the review scope.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance of LLMs in regulated environments, the article has low relevance and limited usable evidence because governance, risk, and monitoring are framed around environmental pollutants rather than conversational AI systems.

synthesis.main_claim: Artificial intelligence and large models can support emerging pollutant identification, real-time risk assessment, intelligent monitoring, and optimization of pollutant governance strategies.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an AI-based framework and a large-model architecture for emerging pollutant governance across screening, risk assessment, and control phases.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance; at most peripheral contextual background on generic large-model governance language in environmental policy.
